scenes.headline: Python UDF
scenes.subtitle: Custom column logic written in plain Python.
scenes.narration: A Python UDF lets you apply custom Python logic to a column when no built-in function will do.

scenes.headline: UDF essentials
items: Wrap a Python function and declare its return type
Applies your logic row by row
Slower because data crosses into the Python process
Use only when built-in functions cannot express it
scenes.narration: You wrap a Python function and declare its return type to make a UDF. It applies your logic row by row, but it is slower because each row crosses into a separate Python process, so reserve it for logic built-ins cannot express.

scenes.headline: Defining and using a UDF
scenes.narration: We decorate a plain Python function with udf and declare it returns a string. The function assigns pass or fail based on the score, and we apply it with withColumn so every row gets a grade computed by our custom logic.

scenes.text: Python UDFs are a last resort — prefer built-in functions, then Pandas UDFs.
scenes.narration: Treat Python UDFs as a last resort: prefer built-in functions first, and vectorized Pandas UDFs before a plain row-at-a-time one.
